thread:
nina: Quick design review on the catalog compare panel — noticed a few interaction surprises when a user "pins" a model version. tagging @kim + @carlos for decisions. :wave:

carlos: steps to repro?

nina: Catalog -> pick two entries -> Compare -> click the pin glyph on the left row. The visual pinned item gets pulled to the top, but keyboard focus snaps out of the panel. reproduces on Chrome + NVDA.

jo: that sounds like a DOM reparenting problem. Are we actually moving the node or recreating it at the top?

nina: code does a remove+prepend to the pinned group so the pinned rows are grouped visually. snippet: `if (v.pinned) pinnedGroup.prepend(row)` — easy but destructive.

kim: design preference: avoid moving interactive elements. two possible patterns: (A) keep DOM order, use CSS (sticky/transform) to visually place pinned rows in a top anchor; (B) render a visual-only pinned header (mirror) while original stays in flow. Which is better for engineering?

carlos: engineering: A is nicest—no clones/event mapping needed. But sticky can be tricky with virtualized lists. B works but clones must be inert to avoid duplicated tab stops (`aria-hidden="true"` + `tabindex="-1"`).

a11y-helper: Important: moving focusable nodes breaks screen reader focus and may announce unexpected changes. If we use clones, ensure clones are non-interactive and that screen readers only ever focus the canonical row. Also, announce the change succinctly: `role="status"` -> "Pinned v2.0.1".

jo: virtualization makes sticky hard because items outside the viewport may unmount. If we want sticky with virtual lists, we need to pin a serialized representation (a small sticky header) that is driven by state, not DOM movement. That ends up close to B but simpler: render a sticky header component that reads the pinned state and displays a summary.

nina: I like the header summary idea: sticky header shows small row chips for pinned versions; original rows remain where they are. Keeps tab order and don't duplicate tabbable elements.

kim: microcopy: current tooltip says "Pin version" which some users thought was toggling the whole compare view. Proposed change: button label = "Pin"; tooltip = "Keep this version visible in comparisons"; toast on pin = "Pinned vX.Y.Z — Undo". Short, actionable.

carlos: agree. engineering note: make toast `aria-live="polite"` and include an Undo button that is keyboard accessible. Also provide an inline `role=status` for immediate SR announce when toggling via keyboard.

a11y-helper: Good. Also, the perf badge tooltip gets clipped when the pinned summary is near the panel edge. Mount tooltips in a portal to `document.body` or ensure container overflow is visible. Add `aria-label` to badges e.g., `aria-label="Latency p95 420ms"`.

jo: Regarding perf badges, can we show inline numbers in the summary to reduce tooltip reliance? e.g., show `p50 120ms • p95 420ms` under the badge icon. That helps discoverability and reduces hover dependency.

nina: Layout question: should pinned summary rows be interactive? If they are, keyboard focus should jump to the canonical row, not the summary. Maybe make summary interactive only for pointer users and non-focusable for keyboard.

carlos: implement summary as a button with `tabindex="-1"` and `aria-hidden="true"` for SRs, but listen to clicks and forward to the canonical row via a programmatic focus call. Hmm that might be weird for keyboard users.

a11y-helper: Don't make interactive controls non-focusable. That breaks keyboard expectations. Better: keep summary non-interactive display (read-only) and include a clear "Go to version" action in the canonical flow. If pointer users click the summary, focus the canonical row and open details. For keyboard users, they should tab to the row normally.

kim: design decision leaning: pinned summary = visual read-only anchor (no tabbable elements). canonical row remains the source-of-truth for interactions. Add a visual divider and subtle shadow so users know it's anchored.

jo: engineering plan: (1) remove DOM reparenting; (2) add `PinnedSummary` component at top of compare panel that reads pinned IDs from state and renders inert visual chips with small metrics; (3) mount tooltips to body; (4) add `role=status` live update when pin toggles; (5) scope state updates so filters/compare shortcuts don't re-render top-level UI unexpectedly.

nina: QA notes: test keyboard-only flow, NVDA/VoiceOver, filter preset stability after pin, tooltip clipping edge cases, and that shortcut (g then c) stays in compare panel. Also verify toasts announce once.

carlos: I'll prototype the `PinnedSummary` and the sticky header approach. If virtualization blocks visuals, fallback to a portal-anchored fixed element. Will include percentiles in the summary numbers.

kim: small copy tweak for the toast undo: instead of "Undo", use "Undo pin" for clarity. Also add accessibility label to the pin button: `aria-pressed` reflecting state and `aria-label` e.g., `"Pin vX.Y.Z"` so screen readers know which version.

a11y-helper: Final checklist for PR: no DOM moves of interactive nodes, `role=status` for pin toggles, toast with `aria-live=polite` and keyboard-accessible undo, tooltips portalled to body, perf badges include accessible labels and optionally inline percentiles, pinned summary is non-focusable read-only, and filters don't lose `aria-pressed` state on pin.

nina: great. I'll drop screenshots and a tiny CSS patch for tooltip portals in the PR comment. leaving this thread open for followups. :thumbsup:
